authority.quote_note: Question tariffs are quoted from the mark scheme's own 'Mark Scheme Assessment Objectives (AO) Grid' (final page), column order Question | AO1 | AO2 | AO3 | AO4 | Total, and from the printed per-question tariffs in the Section B tables ('36+4').

total.why: The AO grid's Totals row. The three question tariffs also sum to it: 20 + 20 + 40 = 80.

questions.quote_note: The grid row for part (a) of every Section A choice (candidates answer on ONE studied poetry cluster, so 1a OR 2a OR 3a). Part (a) compares a named poem from the studied anthology with an UNSEEN poem, marked holistically. Six levels: 18–20 / 15–17 / 11–14 / 7–10 / 4–6 / 1–3. Rubric rule worth teaching, verbatim: 'Where a candidate has only referred to one poem, either the taught or the unseen, the mark awarded is unlikely to move beyond Level 2 and cannot move beyond Level 3.'

components.label: analysis of language, form and structure (AO2)

questions.quote_note: The grid row for part (b): a response on a second poem from the studied anthology, AO1 10 + AO2 10, marked holistically. Six levels: 18–20 / 15–17 / 11–14 / 7–10 / 4–6 / 1–3. No spec_key of its own — literature-paper-specs.json carries ONE ocr.poetry_anthology entry (20 marks, AO1+AO2), which describes both parts; Q1 above is keyed to it.

Locator: the Section B heading, so this question's region covers the Shakespeare level descriptors and every set-text question table. Candidates answer ONE question from the eight (one extract-based and one discursive per play); each table prints its tariff as '36+4' — 36 content marks on the six level descriptors (Level 6 = 31–36) plus 4 AO4 marks on the separate 'Marking Grid for AO4 – SPaG (1–4 marks)'. The final AO grid gives the same total as AO1 14 + AO2 14 + AO3 8 + AO4 4 = 40. Rubric rules worth teaching, verbatim: 'Where a candidate has not moved beyond the extract, the mark awarded cannot move beyond Level 3' and 'Where a candidate has only referred to one moment from the text, the mark awarded cannot move beyond Level 3. Where a candidate has referred briefly to a second moment, the mark cannot move beyond Level 4.'

components.label: content (AO1 + AO2 + AO3)
components.quote_note: Every Section B question table prints '36+4' beside the question. 36 = AO1 14 + AO2 14 + AO3 8, the marks the six level descriptors cover (Level 6 = 31–36).

components.label: spelling, punctuation and grammar (AO4)
components.quote_note: The '+4' in the same printed tariff — awarded on the separate 'Marking Grid for AO4 – SPaG (1–4 marks)'.
